To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Cambrian diversification of the blastozoan subphylum was related to a high turnover rate, a high endemicity and a high origination rate, whereas the Ordovician rise in diversity is related to a low endemicity, a low turnover rate and a low origination rate.

the early Palaeo-zoic diversification of the blastozoans is related with two different faunal assemblages, the Cambrian Evolutionary Faunae and the Palaeozoic evolutionary fauna, which were driven by different evolutionary processes.

the early Palaeo-zoic blastozoan diversification can be divided into three phases: a first Cambrian phase, with a high origination rate and a high endemism, followed by a second Ordovician phase, with a low origination rate and low endemism, and finally a third post-Hirnantian phase, with a medium originations rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a global pattern of diversification and the influence of extrinsic and intrinsic (evolutionary) factors on early Palaeozoan blastozoan diversity.
the evolution of the diversity of a group of organisms, the blastozoans.
the evolution of the early Palæozoic blastozoans, a major component of the Palaeozoic marine ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cambrian diversification was mainly driven by intrinsic processes, while the Ordovician-Silurian diversification was mainly extrinsically driven.
Cambrian and Ordovician diversifications are related to extrinsic (environmental and palaeogeographical) factors, while the Silurian one is related to intrinsic (evolutionary) factors.

the early Palaeoic diversification of echinoderms was driven by both extrinsic (global and local palaeogeographic and environmental/climatic changes) and intrinsic (evolutionary processes) factors, but the relative influence of each factor varied through time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Cambrian diversification of blastozoa was mainly related to intrinsic factors (i.e. evolution of global environmental conditions, and the geographic distribution and evolution of continental masses) and the Ordovician one to extrinsic factors (i.e., geographic extension of blastozoa on most palaeo-continental margins, associated with the gradual sea level rise during the Ordovician).
the early Palaeozioc diversification of the blastozoan fauna was a complex process, driven by both extrinsic and intrinsic processes.

the early Cambrian diversification was driven by the rapid evolution of the Cambrian Evolutionary Faunal assemblage in a context of a rapid sea level rise, whereas the Late Ordovican diversification was driven mainly by the progressive colonisation of different palaeocontinental provinces by the Palaeozoic Faunal assemblages in a context of long-term gradual sea levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a better understanding of the palaeogeographic patterns of the Early Palaeozoic can help to decipher the evolutionary history of blastozoan groups.
, in the early Palæozoic, the diversification pattern and the evolution of the blastozoans was not only controlled by intrinsic factors, but also by extrinsic factors.
, in the early Palæozoic, the diversification of blastozoa is mainly driven by extrinsic factors, i.e. environmental/climatic and geographic factors.
